answer.rationale: The 18% mandate and non-auto-renewing contract force a decision now, and only the low-cost vendor quote meets the mandate outright, making switch_primary_vendor the action most aligned with the primary objective on cost. However, memory_c2's claim of quick, accurate onboarding is the sole basis for believing this won't raise delivery risk, and it was consolidated a year ago under unknown volume/capacity conditions—critically, the line is now at 94% of committed volume with zero buffer, so any onboarding friction could cause a missed delivery with no slack to absorb it. I want to verify c2's original source to see whether onboarding speed and invoicing accuracy were tested under comparable volume pressure or shortage conditions, since that materially changes whether switching now is safe versus whether a guarded parallel test (start second-sourcing or negotiate incumbent terms first) is the wiser sequencing. Given capacity for only one action this cycle, I'm leaning toward switching but scoped as a small guarded test (partial volume shift) rather than a full cutover, preserving the incumbent as fallback until delivery performance is confirmed under real load.
